items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: The interviewee discusses the 'Ball House men' as a group or style associated with musicians like Joe Oliver in the Armand Brass band, but does not describe a direct personal relationship with the collective entity 'Ball House men'.

ctx.x: You should hear those bands in those days, like the Olympia band, Superior band, and Imperial band, those was bands. And the parade, does he like the Armand Brass band? I mean, well, the Armand Brass band, I mean, they played my father, I mean, he can't tell you about that, because you didn't ask him about that. But I can tell you, they played ball house music. You can forget about what he said about the other fellas, you know, reading at that time. Yeah, but later on in the years, I mean, it was a Ball House…
Who were the Ball House men in that band?

Who was the Ball House men in that band? Joe Oliver. He was the man. Joe Oliver, you know, he played, you know, like you have a third trumpet player on the end in the orchestra. Well, that's where Joe was in that band. But Manuel, I mean, he was just a, he made tunes, but you know, good tunes, but not like Joe. Joe was always, I mean, Joe was always like, you know, Ball House, like Lil Armstrong or Buddy Boll or something like that. You know, people like that.
